# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

You implement **one step** of an approved Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Not the next step, not
an improvement you noticed on the way — one step.

**Report in "ELI5BITFEDLOTP" register** — Explain Like I'm 5, But I'm The FED Lead Of The
Project. Not dumbed down, but no jargon in the way: consequence first, then mechanism, then fix.
Marcel reads your report as often as the skill that called you does.

**Scale to the work.** The plan states the scale it chose — honour it, and do not quietly
restore machinery it dropped. Over-scaled effort is a defect, not thoroughness. Two hard stops:
**never re-run an angle or a check against a diff that has not changed since you last ran it**,
and never re-present a conclusion that has not changed. Both have happened here — one session
re-ran an identical four-angle wave ninety minutes later with no commits in between, then ran a
further wave to validate that one.

## Before you write anything

1. Confirm you are **not** on `develop` or `main`. A `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit on those branches; if you are on one, stop and say so rather than working around it.
2. Read the step's file manifest and its pass criteria. Those are your definition of done.

## How you work

- **Only touch files the step names.** If the work genuinely cannot be completed without touching
  a file the plan didn't anticipate, **stop and report it**. Do not decide for yourself.
- **A `findings.md` 🟡 CLARIFY assumption that turns out not to hold, or any conflict you discover
  between the AC text, a Jira comment, and the Figma design that the plan didn't already resolve,
  is Marcel's call, not yours.** Stop and report it for ratification. Do not silently pick a
  resolution and record the judgment call only as a docblock comment — a comment explaining a
  choice is not the same as the choice having been authorised.
- **Never stage and never commit.** No `git add`, no `git commit`, no `git checkout`, no `git
  stash`. Leave your changes in the working tree — the skill owns the commit, and it only commits
  a step the Scorer has passed and Marcel has eyeballed.
- **Copy-first is not optional.** Overriding a base SFCC file means: copy it verbatim to the
  mirrored path, convert `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`, replace `PropTypes` with real types
  (no `any`, no `@ts-ignore`), get `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, prove the override renders — and
  **then stop and present before making any functional change.**
- **Import an already-overridden component by relative path**, never by its
  `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` base path. A base-path import compiles and ships fine but
  silently renders the *unstyled base component* in Storybook and Vitest, because the
  `ccExtensibility` resolver only runs in the real webpack build.
- **Never assert a rule, pattern, or precedent exists in this codebase without citing the exact
  `file:line` that says so.** If a docblock needs to justify a design decision by reference to an
  existing convention and you cannot point to the specific line making that claim, the citation is
  invented — stop and report the decision as needing Marcel's call, rather than writing a
  justification that merely sounds plausible.
- **Never describe a later step in the same plan as already done.** A comment referencing what a
  future step will do belongs in future tense ("will be removed in step E4") or flagged as
  not-yet-run — not phrased as settled fact ahead of time. This recurred twice in one build
  (SFCC-83+84-einstein, 2026-09-15) before being caught: two separate docblocks each described
  a step that hadn't run yet as if it already had.
- **Never reuse a specific number from an existing comment (a measurement, a pixel value, a
  claimed line-height) in new logic without independently verifying it against the real
  rendered/computed value first.** An existing citation can be stale, wrong, or describing
  something adjacent to what it's being reused for (e.g. a Figma auto-layout reading is not the
  same thing as a real CSS line-height) — treat it as a claim to check, not a fact to build on.
- Follow the styling hierarchy: `textStyle` → `var(--zimm-*)` → theme recipe → `sx` → scoped
  `.scss`. Never a bare Chakra token key. Never a raw hex/px/rem/em in a component file — if a
  value genuinely has no token yet, make it a **named constant** with a comment containing
  `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder` or `audit-allow: <reason>`, never an inline literal.
- Name new recipes `Zimm*` and register them in `theme/components/index.ts`.
- A component exported from its folder needs a story. A component with real logic needs its own
  test file.

## When you finish the step

Run and report the output of:

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test
```

`npm run test` includes `recipeGuards.test.ts`, which is the hard styling gate — five guards that
fail the build on bare token keys, unnamespaced recipes, and unregistered recipes. If it fails,
fix it before reporting done; that failure is yours, not the loop's.

Report what you changed, file by file, and the evidence for each pass criterion. Do not claim a

146	| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/{index.tsx,index.test.tsx,index.stories.tsx}` | **modify** | Tier 3 (`ui-kits/`, same CODEOWNERS routing as every other file in this table) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` <!-- added 2026-09-21: a real, in-scope Design-fidelity fix found and made during this step's own build (index.stories.tsx added to this row after its own Tester found hideLabelVisually had zero story coverage) — Figma's Apple Pay/Google Pay buttons are icon-only (confirmed via a live get_screenshot pull of the real button-group frame), but ZimmButton's primary/secondary path had no way to supply a real accessible name without also rendering it as visible text. Added `hideLabelVisually` (VisuallyHidden on true, unconditional aria-label unchanged either way) — same shape as the already-accepted `ariaDescribedBy`-on-icon-variant precedent from an earlier step. Same tier as everything else in this table, not a multi-tier escalation. --> |
147	| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | modify | **Tier 2** | `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers` |
148	
149	### Not in this manifest, on purpose
150	
151	`overrides/app/theme/foundation/**` — **untouched**. Gate finding #13's caption-weight override happens in the component recipe. Every cart colour already exists (`grey[900]`, `grey[600]`, `grey[300]`, `red[500]`, `green[500]`, `ivory[200]`, `grey[100]`). Zero new tokens. If any step reaches for `foundation/`, the step is wrong.
152	
153	`.claude/registry/*.md` — regenerated by `npm run generate:registry`, which writes into `.claude/`, inside my no-plan scope. See open question 9.
154	
155	---
156	
157	## 4. Steps
158	
159	Mechanical gates referenced below, run on every step: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npm run lint` clean · `npm run test` green (this is what runs `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token + `Zimm*`-namespacing guards, `recipeParts.test.ts`'s parts-vs-reads guard, and `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision guard) · `npm run audit:tokens` reports no new finding in the touched paths.
160	
161	Styling rules every step inherits: `textStyle` → `var(--zimm-*)` → recipe → `sx` → `.scss`. Never a bare Chakra key. Never a raw hex/px/rem/em in a component file. Responsive steps are explicit media queries off `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation` — the pattern `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already uses; do **not** add a third `BP` alias alongside `footerShared.ts`'s and `headerShared.ts`'s. Never Chakra's array shorthand in a recipe.
162	
163	**Figma space-token mapping:** resolve each `alias/space/NNNN` to the named `--zimm-scale-*` step with the same px value; only seven numeric aliases exist (`025`, `700`, `1100`, `1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`), so verify each against `foundation/spacing.ts` and `foundation/zimmTokens.ts` before typing it rather than inferring from the number. Per §11.10(9), **use the token value, never Figma's decimal** — `12.655` and `8.944` are post-scale render artefacts of `space/1200` (48px) and `space/1000` (40px).
164	
165	**No hover-reveal surface exists in this bundle** — the cart item's action links are always visible in every Figma frame. If one appears during build, it is `:hover, :has(:focus-visible)`, never `:focus-within`.
166	
167	---
168	
169	### B0 — Step 0: `cart` e2e area
170	
171	**Changes.** Add a `cart` path group to `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` `Get changed files` step, matching the six globs listed in the manifest, and wire it into `Compute E2E scope` the same way `e2e_homepage` is.
172	
173	**Pass criteria.**
174	1. `gh api user --jq .login` returns a login present in `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members --jq '.[].login'`, **or** a named approving review is secured first. Recorded in the PR body either way.
175	2. `actionlint`/YAML parse clean; the workflow appears in `gh workflow list`.
176	3. On the next cart PR, the `detect-changes` job's `e2e_scope` output is literally `cart`, not `skip` and not `full`.
177	4. With no `@cart`-tagged spec yet present, `e2e-localhost` reports "no tests found" and **passes** — not fails. (`testing.md` documents this as a free no-op.)
178	5. `e2e_homepage` scoping is unchanged: a homepage-only PR still resolves to `homepage`.
179	
180	**Skill.** None. Direct edit.
181	
182	**Known limit, state it in the PR body:** B1 touches the shared `zimmDrawer` atom, so B1's own PR will still resolve to `e2e_scope: skip`. The area helps B3/B4/B5, not B1.
183	
184	---
185	
186	### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism
187	
188	#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)
189	
190	**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.
191	
192	**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.
193	
194	**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.
195	
196	**Pass criteria.**
197	1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
198	2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
199	3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
200	4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).
201	
202	#### Step 1.2 — `ZimmCartDrawer` organism
203	
204	**Changes.** New organism at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/`, wrapping `ZimmDrawer` with `size="xLarge"`. Props only — `isOpen`, `onClose`, `itemCount`, `finalFocusRef`, `children`, plus a `messages` slot and a `footer` slot (the footer slot is what hosts SFCC-275's button group until SFCC-816 lands). Recipe `ZimmCartDrawer` with parts for the messages band, the content container, and the two-column/one-column grid.
205	
206	Header title: `"BAG • {count}"` via `ZimmDrawer`'s existing `title` prop (AC1). Empty: `"YOUR BAG IS EMPTY"` — **header text only**; the empty *body* is SFCC-277's and arrives in B4 as a slotted component.
207	
208	The 52px messages band reserves its height while empty (designer annotation §11.3.1, "to prevent the cart changing position depending on errors") — `minHeight` on the `messagesBand` part. Resolve 52px to its `--zimm-scale-*` step; do not type `52px`.
209	
210	Layout per §11.10's derived responsive rule: desktop ≥1440 two columns (items 360 / totals 430 / 140 gutter, 128 page gutter, header 84); tablet 834 single column, **fluid width with a 32px gutter — never the computed 659.2**; mobile full-width single column, 32px gutter. Header height: **whatever `ZimmDrawer` already implements** — §11.11(3) is explicit that its sizing was reconciled with the designer during SFCC-831/926 and the cart nodes disagree with each other (108 vs 68).
211	
212	**Pass criteria.**
213	1. Story `Default` renders with `itemCount={3}` and the header reads exactly `BAG • 3`.
214	2. Story `Empty` renders and the header reads exactly `YOUR BAG IS EMPTY`; the messages band is still present in the DOM with a resolved `min-height` equal to the 52px token (assert in `zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts`, not by eyeballing the story).
215	3. `index.test.tsx` asserts: Escape calls `onClose`; backdrop click calls `onClose`; close button calls `onClose`; after close, focus is on the element passed as `finalFocusRef` (AC7).
216	4. `index.test.tsx` asserts scroll position is **restored**, not merely unlocked, on close (AC8 — the note flags this specifically as needing verification rather than assumption).
217	5. `zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts` asserts the two-column grid above the desktop breakpoint and single-column at and below tablet, each as an explicit media query, and that the tablet step carries a 32px gutter token with no `659.2` anywhere in the file.
218	6. `recipeParts.test.ts` passes — every part read off `useMultiStyleConfig` in `index.tsx` is declared in the recipe's `parts`.
219	7. Recipe key is `ZimmCartDrawer` (namespaced) and registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.
220	8. Story `title` is `'Layout/ZimmCartDrawer'` per `components.md`'s categorisation (global chrome/structural).
221	9. Storybook a11y check passes on both stories (it is gated in `preview.tsx` — do not disable it).
222	
223	**Skill.** `/new-component` for the scaffold.
224	
225	---
226	
227	### B2 — SFCC-270, copy-first override
228	
229	#### Step 2.1 — Copy-first, then STOP
230	
231	**Changes.** Copy all eight base files verbatim to their mirrored paths, convert each to `.tsx`, update imports, add a `console.log('[overrides] <filename>')` marker to each.
232	
233	Sources:
234	- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/{index,bonus-product-quantity,product-quantity-picker}.jsx`
235	- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/{index,item-image,item-name,item-attributes,item-price}.jsx`
236	
237	Do **not** copy the base `.test.js`/`.test.jsx` or `data.mock.js` — we write our own.
238	
239	**Pass criteria.**
240	1. All eight files exist at their mirrored `overrides/` paths with `.tsx` extensions. Zero `.jsx` under `overrides/`.
241	2. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
242	3. **Zero functional diff.** `git diff --no-index` between each base `.jsx` and its converted `.tsx`, ignoring type annotations, import-path rewrites and the marker line, shows no logic change. The defaults-then-spread order in `item-image`, `item-attributes` and `item-price` is untouched at this step. The `item-name` bug fix is **step 2.2**, not here.
243	4. `product-item/index.tsx`'s internal imports of `item-variant/*` are rewritten to **relative paths** (`'../item-variant/item-image'`), not the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path. This is the interception rule from `overrideStyling.md` — the base path builds and runs correctly in the app but silently renders the **unstyled base** in Storybook and Vitest, because `.storybook/main.js` aliases the package straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it. Get this wrong and every story and test in B3 will be exercising base SFCC, not our override, and look fine doing it.
244	5. `product-item/index.tsx`'s imports of modules it is **not** also overriding (`shared/ui`, `responsive`, `loading-spinner`, `quantity-picker`, `utils/utils`, `hooks`) stay on the base path. The `shared/ui` barrel trap applies — do not attempt to override individual `shared/ui/<Name>` members; 208 base files import the barrel.
245	6. **STOP.** Present the eight files to Marcel. Confirm in the running app that each marker logs — including from the wishlist page and a checkout summary, not just the cart — before any functional change. Then remove the markers.
246	
247	**Skill.** `/override-component`, if it exists in `.claude/skills/`; otherwise the copy-first rule in AGENTS.md directly.
248	
249	#### Step 2.2 — Restyle to Figma + the `item-name` fix
250	
251	**Changes.** Co-located recipes `product-item/product-item.css.ts` (exporting `ZimmCartItem`) and `item-variant/item-variant.css.ts` (exporting `ZimmCartItemVariant`). Replace `layerStyle="cardBordered"` and the Chakra array-shorthand geometry (`width={['88px','136px']}`, `display={['none','block',...]}`) with recipe parts and explicit media queries.
252	
253	Figma values (§11.2): root gap 28px desktop / 24px mobile, align `center` desktop / `start` mobile; image group 132×198 desktop `object-cover` / 67×100 mobile `object-contain`, aspect 288/432, bg `ivory[200]`, `mix-blend-multiply`; Item Details gap 12px desktop / 24px mobile; Item Info column desktop / row-space-between mobile. Product name **uppercase**, `textStyle="productNames"`. Price `textStyle="price"`. Colour + size as **one combined string** ("Lilac Sand, One size"), 200px wide, `text.secondary` — SFCC-270's separate colour AC and size AC are **two ACs describing one element**, so do not build two nodes.
254	
255	The regular-weight 12px caption (Figma `Default/Caption`) has no textStyle — gate finding #13. Use `textStyle="caption"` and override `fontWeight` to regular **in the recipe**, annotated. Do not add a textStyle to `foundation/typography.ts`; that is Tier 1 from a cart ticket.
256	
257	Two load-bearing requirements from the decision record:
258	- **Keep defaults-then-spread.** `<Box width={zimmDefault} {...props}>`, never the reverse. `order-summary` calls `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` and must keep winning.
259	- **Fix `item-name`.** Base is `<Link {...props} color="black.600">` — spread before the colour, so no caller can ever override it. Move the spread after. No base caller passes `color`, so nothing changes for them.
260	
261	Make the stepper slot and the actions slot **optional** on the override's render path — the digital gift-card variant has neither (§11.2). Physical gift cards render as a standard 198 item.
262	
263	**Pass criteria.**
264	1. `product-item/index.test.tsx` asserts, with the line item mocked: image renders with an `alt`; name renders uppercase; price renders; the combined colour+size string renders as **one** text node containing both values.
265	2. `item-variant/index.test.tsx` asserts a caller-passed `width` on `CartItemVariantImage` **wins** over the Zimmermann default, and the same for `mr`. This is the regression that breaks `order-summary` if the spread order flips.
266	3. A test asserts `CartItemVariantName` accepts and applies a caller-passed `color` — proving the base bug is fixed and provable, not asserted.
267	4. Rendering `product-item` with no stepper and no actions produces neither in the DOM and throws nothing (gift-card API requirement).
268	5. `recipeGuards.test.ts` passes: recipe keys are `ZimmCartItem` / `ZimmCartItemVariant` (`Zimm*`-namespaced, so they cannot deep-merge with a base recipe), and no bare Chakra token key appears on a registered scale.
269	6. `recipeParts.test.ts` passes for both recipes.
270	7. `npm run audit:tokens` reports no new raw hex/px/rem/em in `product-item/` or `item-variant/`.
271	8. `grep -n "\[" product-item/index.tsx` shows no Chakra responsive array shorthand remaining in geometry props.
272	9. Stories exist at `Commerce/ProductItem` with `Default`, `GiftCard` (no stepper/actions), and `MultipleItems` variants.
273	10. Mobile: at 402px viewport in the story, nothing truncated or hidden (AC9) — assert no `text-overflow: ellipsis` and no `display: none` on name, price, colour/size, stepper or actions.
274	
275	---
276	
277	### B3 — SFCC-795 + 271, states and stepper
278	
279	#### Step 3.1 — `ZimmQuantityStepper` molecule
280	
281	**Changes.** New molecule composing two `ZimmButton`s at `size="icon"` around a value display. Gap **8px (`xs`)** per §11.11(1) — design showed a 12px gap around a 12px glyph with no touch target; we apply the system's 24px `minW`/`minH` (ZimmButton `icon` already is `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`), which adds 6px invisible padding each side, so 8px yields 14px apparent. Annotate exactly that, citing WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 and the Figma node literally named `touchTarget` at 24.
282	
283	Disabled glyphs use `OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4` from `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmCartItemShared.ts` — Figma ships separate greyed SVGs; we use opacity. One constant, one file, read by both the recipe and the tests.
284	
285	**Pass criteria — every state named, because a state absent here is absent from the Tester's brief and the Scorer's gate:**
286	1. Quantity 1: `−` is `disabled`, carries `aria-disabled` or the native attribute, renders at 0.4 opacity; clicking it does nothing and quantity stays 1 (AC3).
287	2. Quantity > 1: both enabled; `−` decrements by exactly 1; `+` increments by exactly 1 (ACs 1, 2).
288	3. Quantity at max: `+` disabled and greyed, `−` still enabled (795 stepper group).
289	4. Fully OOS or unavailable: **both** disabled and greyed (795 stepper group).
290	5. **Hover, focus-visible and active** are inherited from `ZimmButton`'s `icon` variant, which already carries `_hover`/`_focusVisible`/`_active`/`_disabled`. Assert in the recipe test that the focus-visible ring's resolved value is **not identical to the default state** — an invisible focus state is a WCAG 2.4.7 failure and is the exact bug `zimmButton.css.ts` records having already shipped once. Figma supplies no hover/focus node for the stepper; inheritance is the resolution, annotated at the point of use. Do not invent a value.
291	6. Each button has an `aria-label` (`IconButton` renders no visible text — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`).
292	7. Resolved target size of each control is ≥24×24 CSS px, asserted from the recipe, not measured in a browser.
293	8. `index.stories.tsx` has a `play` covering increment, decrement, and the disabled-at-1 boundary.
294	
295	#### Step 3.2 — `ZimmInlineMessage` atom + error/warning states
296	
297	**Changes.** New atom, variant-driven: `error` (`status.error`) / `warning` (`text.muted`). It sits **between the stepper and the actions row**, full width, `textStyle="caption"` with weight overridden to regular per gate #13. In error states the Item Details gap widens 12 → 16px — that is a recipe state on `ZimmCartItem`, not a prop on the message.
298	
299	**Presentation only.** OOS / partial OOS triggering is SFCC-282 and Unavailable is SFCC-796 — both Sprint 6, Hazel's. Build prop-driven with stories; do not wire detection logic.
300	
301	Copy, verbatim from Figma: fully OOS **"This item is unavailable"**; partial OOS **"Quantity unavailable in this size"**; max quantity **"Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size"**.
302	
303	Per gate #4, max-quantity renders as the **warning** variant (grey, `text.muted`), not error — the design and SFCC-250 AC4 agree; CAI-017's word "error" means user-facing feedback, not the severity tier. Annotate that reconciliation inline.
304	
305	Per gate #9, **there is no low-stock variant** — CAI-030 forbids low-stock messaging at cart level. Do not add one.
306	
307	**Pass criteria.**
308	1. Stories: `Error`, `Warning`, plus one per copy string above. Each renders the exact copy.
309	2. `error` resolves to `var(--zimm-color-status-error)`; `warning` to `var(--zimm-color-text-muted)`. Both asserted in the recipe test against the token var, not a hex.
310	3. The organism recipe test asserts Item Details gap is the 12px token by default and the 16px token in the error state.
311	4. Message renders in DOM order **between** stepper and actions.
312	5. No `#9c0000`, `#969696` or any hex literal in either file — `npm run audit:tokens` clean.
313	6. No low-stock variant exists in the component's variant union.
314	
315	#### Step 3.3 — Promotional price + discount label
316	
317	**Changes.** The was/now mechanism **already exists** in base `display-price` (`priceData` with `listPrice`/`currentPrice`/`isOnSale`, renders `ListPrice` struck, already multiplies by quantity so it is line-item aware). Only the **discount label** ("20% off applied") is new, and it is purely presentational — prop-driven, storied, wired when the promotions engine lands. It renders beneath the stepper.
318	
319	`display-price` has **no override** and is a shared SFCC internal. Do not override it in this step; if Zimmermann styling is needed later it goes through the bridge pattern (faithful default export, styling in a recipe).

# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.

---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, now 20 commits** (18 originally; the
> 3.5 stepper-wiring insertion on 2026-09-18 made it 19, the 4.6 cartDrawerContainer insertion on
> 2026-09-20 made it 20 — this line and the other plain "18"/"eighteen" mentions below went stale
> both times and were only just corrected; treat this number as the one to keep current, not
> re-derive from memory, if a further step ever gets inserted).
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |

Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |

### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.

1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.
9. **A green Vitest suite does not prove a `.stories.tsx` file actually renders (added 2026-09-20,
   after step 4.4 shipped four crashing stories through an entire round-0 build, its Tester's Full
   loop, and its own Orchestrator, all green).** `ZimmCartItemActions` called `ZimmLink`, which
   calls `useSafeHref()` unconditionally, which needs a `MultiSiteProvider` the story never
   supplied — every sibling component that already uses `ZimmLink` (`footer`, `zimmSizeSelector`,
   `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`, `zimmLink`'s own story) already carries the decorator this one
   was missing. `index.test.tsx`'s own Vitest suite mocked `useSafeHref` away specifically to avoid
   this exact hazard — correctly, for a unit test — which is precisely why it could never have
   caught a *Storybook*-level failure of the same hazard; the two layers were never actually
   testing the same thing. **Any step that creates or meaningfully changes a `.stories.tsx` file
   must actually build and serve Storybook and run `test-storybook --ci` (or equivalent — open each
   changed story in a real browser and confirm no error boundary) before that step can be scored,
   not just read the `play` function and assume it executes.** This is a different failure mode
   than points 1–7 above (which are about a story rendering the *wrong* thing) — this is about
   whether it renders *at all*, and no other gate in this loop checks for it.

## Commit order

The step boundaries in §4 **are** the commit boundaries. That is what keeps a ~60-file PR
reviewable: twenty scoped commits are navigable, three are not. Order matters more than it did
under §2 because there is no merge between stages.

| # | Commit | From §4 step |
|---|---|---|

`commit-msg` enforces conventional format and `/generate-changelog` depends on it, so every message
is `type(scope): SFCC-NNN description`.

**Two things this ordering buys:**

- **Commit 20 puts the trigger last** (was 18 pre-3.5, 19 pre-4.6 — see the note on §2's superseded
  header). Under §2 it had to ship with B1. Here nothing is reachable until everything is built,

- **Commit 4 preserves the copy-first pause intact.** Copy-first was never about branching — it is
  about not bundling the override copy with functional change. Commit 4 stops and waits for

  summary. Nothing proceeds until that is recorded.

## Loop, restated per commit group

§5's per-step Tester/Scorer criteria stand verbatim. Only the per-branch scaling is replaced:

| Commits | Loop |
|---|---|
| 1 | None. Verified by reading `detect-changes`'s output on the next cart PR. |
| 2, 3 | Light — a path check and a width assertion. |
| 4 | **Mandatory human stop.** The one step a machine cannot score alone. |

| 13–17 | Full loop, and **commit 14 gets the only adversarial pass** — concurrency, double-write, server rejection, boundary at 2/3/4/5, and proving `useIsMutating()` by making it fail on purpose first. |
| 18 | Light. |
| 19 | Full loop — the actual cart-content assembly (step 4.6, inserted 2026-09-20): `useCartMergeAndCap`'s render guard, `useCartMessages`, `ZimmCartItemActions` and `ZimmCartEmptyState` all get wired together for the first time here. Treat with the same care 3.5's insertion got — a wiring mistake here is exactly as invisible to any single piece's own per-file review as that one was. |
| 20 | Light on the trigger swap itself, but **carries a regression check**, not a light pass: `product-view` is consumed by the PDP, the quick-view modal and the bonus-product modal, and this commit changes their add-to-bag feedback. |

     concurrency/useIsMutating step, confirmed by both this step's Orchestrator and Scorer), 19 =

     commit from 19 to 20, and added 19 as its own new row (the assembly step) above. The commit
     numbers cited in this comment's own prose (12, 14) are unaffected — both sit before the 4.6
     insertion point — only the "19 = final wiring commit" claim at the end was stale; it's 20 now,

## Costs accepted by choosing one PR

   B3/B4/B5 coverage.

   (`_app/`, `product-item/`, `theme/components/index.ts`), `@pwa-squad-a` and `@pwa-squad-b`;

   dashboard. `e2e-browserstack-preview`'s `--grep` OR-joins all seven keys correctly, so scoping
   still works.

## PR body requirement

A ~60-file, seven-story PR is unverifiable without a body that maps **story → commits → files →
ACs**. That is `zimmerMANNPostBuild`'s deliverable and it is real work — budget it rather than
discover it at the end. Note the recorded PR-body standard says *no SFCC key in the title* while

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { ZimmDrawer } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer';
4	
5	const ZIMM_CART_DRAWER_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartDrawer';
6	
7	export type ZimmCartDrawerProps = {
8	  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
9	  isOpen: boolean;
10	  /** Called on backdrop click, Escape, and the close button (all via ZimmDrawer/Chakra's Drawer). */
11	  onClose: () => void;
12	  /** Number of line items in the bag. Drives the header title only ("BAG • {itemCount}" vs
13	   *  "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY") — see `children`'s own doc below for the empty-vs-populated body. */
14	  itemCount: number;
15	  /** Element to focus once the drawer finishes closing — see ZimmDrawer's own doc (AC10
16	   *  focus-return); without this Chakra falls back to focusing document.body. */
17	  finalFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
18	  /** Cart line items — or the empty-state body. This organism owns no item-rendering logic and
19	   *  no empty-vs-populated decision itself: it renders whatever `children` it is given,
20	   *  unconditionally, regardless of `itemCount`. The caller (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, SFCC-11
21	   *  plan step 4.6) decides between the real item list and `ZimmCartEmptyState`. */
22	  children: React.ReactNode;
23	  /** Reserved slot for SFCC-404's message-aggregation system (validation/error/promo banners).
24	   *  Always rendered, even with nothing passed — see zimmCartDrawer.css.ts's `messages` part:
25	   *  the band reserves height regardless, so the drawer doesn't change position when a message
26	   *  appears or disappears. */
27	  messages?: React.ReactNode;
28	  /** Reserved slot for SFCC-275's button group (checkout / continue shopping). Not built in this
29	   *  commit (SFCC-315 is shell-only) — this organism only provides the slot it will render into
30	   *  later. */
31	  footer?: React.ReactNode;
32	};
33	
34	/**
35	 * SFCC-315 — the Cart drawer shell. Wraps ZimmDrawer (size="xLarge") with the cart-specific
36	 * header title, a height-reserving messages band, a responsive items/totals layout, and a
37	 * footer slot.
38	 *
39	 * Deliberately not wired to a trigger yet — no `_app`/`product-view` changes, no
40	 * `useCartDrawer` hook, no button-group content, no message aggregation. Those remain separate,
41	 * later commits in this same plan — this organism is exercised only via its own Storybook
42	 * stories today. (Corrected 2026-09-21, SFCC-11 plan step 4.6: this paragraph used to also list
43	 * "no real empty-state body" here — no longer true. This component itself never owned that
44	 * decision; it renders whatever `children` it is given unconditionally. The real empty-state
45	 * body — deciding between the item list and `ZimmCartEmptyState` — is `cartDrawerContainer.tsx`'s
46	 * job, per `ZimmCartDrawerProps.children`'s own doc above.)
47	 *
48	 * Figma-fidelity audit fix, 2026-09-19: `ZimmDrawer`'s `title` was passed with no `titleStyle`,
49	 * so it silently took that prop's default (`'large'` → `heading1`, 24px) instead of the Figma
50	 * spec for this header ("BAG • #", 14px medium — `body2Strong`). Measured live before the fix:
51	 * 24px/400/32px against the 14px/500 spec. `ZimmDrawer` itself already supports both correctly
52	 * (`titleStyle="small"` → `body2Strong`, confirmed against `typography.ts`) — this was a missing
53	 * prop at the call site, not a defect in `ZimmDrawer`.
54	 *
55	 * @param props see ZimmCartDrawerProps
56	 */
57	export const ZimmCartDrawer = ({
58	  isOpen,
59	  onClose,
60	  itemCount,
61	  finalFocusRef,
62	  children,
63	  messages,
64	  footer,
65	}: ZimmCartDrawerProps) => {
66	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_DRAWER_RECIPE, {});
67	  const title = itemCount === 0 ? 'YOUR BAG IS EMPTY' : `BAG • ${itemCount}`;
68	
69	  return (
70	    <ZimmDrawer
71	      isOpen={isOpen}
72	      onClose={onClose}
73	      size="xLarge"
74	      title={title}
75	      titleStyle="small"
76	      finalFocusRef={finalFocusRef}
77	    >
78	      <chakra.div __css={styles.messages}>{messages}</chakra.div>
79	      {/* SFCC-11 plan step 4.6 fix: this used to be `itemCount === 0 ? <hardcoded placeholder> :
80	          children` — ignoring `children` entirely at zero items, no matter what the caller passed.
81	          Renders `children` unconditionally now; the empty-vs-populated decision belongs entirely
82	          to the caller (see ZimmCartDrawerProps.children's own doc above). */}
83	      <chakra.div __css={styles.body}>{children}</chakra.div>
84	      <chakra.div __css={styles.footer}>{footer}</chakra.div>
85	    </ZimmDrawer>
86	  );
87	};

12	 * the drawer always renders whatever the current basket contains (see `CartDrawerContainer`'s own
13	 * docblock). So the shared state here is just isOpen/onOpen/onClose, and Chakra's own
14	 * `useDisclosure()` — already used for exactly this shape elsewhere in this codebase
15	 * (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:126`) — is the more idiomatic choice than hand-rolling base's raw
16	 * `useState`.
17	 *
18	 * Two real constraints shaped this file, both found by reading the actual current code rather
19	 * than assumed:
20	 *
21	 * 1. **The structural trap base's own code fell into.** `AddToCartModalProvider` is mounted in
22	 *    base `_app` today, but `<AddToCartModal />` itself is never rendered anywhere, base or
23	 *    override (confirmed by grepping the whole `retail-react-app` package) — a component can't
24	 *    easily be both a Context's wrapper and a Context's consumer of its own child in the same
25	 *    render pass, and base's own code never solved that, so add-to-cart has shipped with zero
26	 *    visual feedback. Fixed here by making `CartDrawerProvider` itself render
27	 *    `CartDrawerContainer` (the file that actually renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` with real basket
28	 *    content) — the Provider can never be mounted without the real UI being fed real props,
29	 *    because both happen in the same component body.
30	 *
31	 * 2. **`_app` needs this same live state for its own bag-icon click handler, and `_app` is the
32	 *    component that mounts `CartDrawerProvider`.** A component cannot consume a context it is
33	 *    itself providing within its own subtree — there is no ancestor `CartDrawerProvider` above
34	 *    `_app`'s own top-level code, only a descendant one it's about to render. `useCartDrawerState`
35	 *    is exported separately from `useCartDrawer` so `_app` can call the *raw* state builder
36	 *    directly (the same way it already calls plain `useDisclosure()` directly for its own mobile
37	 *    nav drawer state) and pass the resulting value into `<CartDrawerProvider value={...}>` —
38	 *    so `_app`'s own handler and every nested consumer (`product-view`) always observe the
39	 *    identical live state, never two independent copies. `useCartDrawer()` (the Context reader)
40	 *    is for every other consumer, which — unlike `_app` — genuinely is a descendant of the
41	 *    Provider.
42	 */
43	
44	export type CartDrawerContextValue = {
45	  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
46	  isOpen: boolean;
47	  /**
48	   * Opens the drawer. Pass the element that should receive focus back once the drawer closes
49	   * (AC10) — e.g. the real clicked `<button>`/`<IconButton>` DOM node. Mirrors
50	   * `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `handleTriggerClick` (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:267-276`):
51	   * capture a real element at the moment of the triggering interaction, rather than reading
52	   * `document.activeElement` later — that file's own comment on why
53	   * (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:268-269`) applies identically here: a mouse click does not
54	   * reliably focus the clicked element in every browser. Omit/pass `null`/`undefined` when no
55	   * trigger element is available; the previous trigger (if any) is left untouched rather than
56	   * cleared, so a best-effort focus target is still preferred over none.
57	   */
58	  onOpen: (trigger?: HTMLElement | null) => void;
59	  /** Closes the drawer. Does not clear `triggerRef` — see `handleCloseComplete` in
60	   *  `zimmDrawer/index.tsx`, which reads `finalFocusRef` only after the close animation
61	   *  finishes, i.e. strictly after `onClose` has already run. Clearing the ref here would
62	   *  make AC10 focus-return silently fail on every close. */
63	  onClose: () => void;
64	  /** AC10 focus-return target — whichever element was last passed to `onOpen`. Forward to
65	   *  `ZimmDrawer`/`CartDrawerContainer`'s `finalFocusRef` prop. Typed as `RefObject<HTMLElement>`
66	   *  (not `| null`) to satisfy that prop's own type — same typing precedent as
67	   *  `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `triggerRef` (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:88,140`). */
68	  triggerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement>;
69	};
70	
71	// Exported (not just used internally) for the same reason base exports `AddToCartModalContext`
72	// directly (`use-add-to-cart-modal.js:59`) — lets a test wrap a subtree with a controlled value
73	// via `CartDrawerContext.Provider` directly, without going through the real state builder.
74	export const CartDrawerContext = createContext<CartDrawerContextValue | undefined>(undefined);
75	
76	/**
77	 * Builds the cart drawer's shared isOpen/onOpen/onClose state plus its AC10 focus-return
78	 * trigger ref — the raw equivalent of base's own `useAddToCartModal()`. Called exactly once, by
79	 * `_app`, which passes the result into `CartDrawerProvider`'s `value` prop — see this file's own
80	 * module docblock (constraint 2) for why `_app` needs the raw builder rather than
81	 * `useCartDrawer()`'s Context read.
82	 *
83	 * @returns The shared cart-drawer state — see `CartDrawerContextValue`.
84	 */
85	export const useCartDrawerState = (): CartDrawerContextValue => {
86	  const { isOpen, onOpen: onDisclosureOpen, onClose } = useDisclosure();
87	  // Typed as HTMLElement (not HTMLElement | null) so `.current` is writable below — same cast
88	  // and reasoning as useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:140 (a plain `useRef<HTMLElement>(null)` would
89	  // infer the read-only `RefObject<HTMLElement>` overload instead of `MutableRefObject`).
90	  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null as unknown as HTMLElement);
91	
92	  const onOpen = (trigger?: HTMLElement | null): void => {
93	    if (trigger) triggerRef.current = trigger;
94	    onDisclosureOpen();
95	  };
96	
97	  // Judgement call (no AC or Figma state describes this either way — see this hook's own
98	  // module docblock and the PR report for the fuller reasoning): close the drawer whenever the
99	  // route changes, mirroring base `use-add-to-cart-modal.js`'s own `[pathname]`-keyed effect
100	  // (`use-add-to-cart-modal.js:603-611`) and this exact file's sibling precedent —
101	  // `_app/index.tsx`'s own mobile-nav drawer already closes itself the same way
102	  // (`_app/index.tsx`'s own `useEffect(() => { onClose(); }, [location])`, "Lets automatically
103	  // close the mobile navigation when the location path is changed."). Concretely load-bearing,
104	  // not just consistency: `ZimmCartButtonGroup`'s Checkout button (already built, SFCC-275)
105	  // navigates via a plain `history.push('/checkout')` with no `onClose` call of its own
106	  // (verified directly against `zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx`'s `handleCheckoutClick`), and
107	  // `ZimmDrawer`'s overlay is not click-through — without this effect, clicking Checkout from
108	  // inside the cart drawer would navigate to `/checkout` while the drawer stayed open on top of
109	  // it, leaving the shopper unable to see or reach the page they just navigated to.
110	  const { pathname } = useLocation();
111	  useEffect(() => {
112	    if (isOpen) {
113	      onClose();
114	    }
115	    // Deliberately keyed on pathname alone, matching use-add-to-cart-modal.js's own shape —
116	    // isOpen/onClose are read for their current value, not to decide when the effect re-runs.
117	  }, [pathname]);
118	
119	  return { isOpen, onOpen, onClose, triggerRef };
120	};
121	
122	/**
123	 * Reads the shared cart-drawer state from Context. For any consumer that is a genuine descendant
124	 * of `CartDrawerProvider` (e.g. `product-view`) — see this file's own module docblock for why
125	 * `_app` itself must use `useCartDrawerState()` directly instead. Throws outside a Provider
126	 * (matching `useIntl`'s own real, non-degrading behaviour for the same "this is load-bearing
127	 * business logic, not optional content" reasoning `components.md` documents for that hook) rather
128	 * than silently returning a no-op, since a missing Provider here means add-to-bag feedback is
129	 * broken, not just cosmetically absent.
130	 *
131	 * @returns The shared cart-drawer state — see `CartDrawerContextValue`.
132	 */
133	export const useCartDrawer = (): CartDrawerContextValue => {
134	  const ctx = useContext(CartDrawerContext);
135	  if (!ctx) {
136	    throw new Error('useCartDrawer must be used within a CartDrawerProvider');
137	  }
138	  return ctx;
139	};
140	
141	export type CartDrawerProviderProps = {
142	  /** The live state to provide — built via `useCartDrawerState()` by the one caller (`_app`)
143	   *  that also needs it directly for its own bag-icon click handler. Accepting it as a prop
144	   *  (rather than calling `useCartDrawerState()` internally) is what lets `_app` and every
145	   *  nested consumer share the exact same instance — see this file's own module docblock,
146	   *  constraint 2. */
147	  value: CartDrawerContextValue;
148	  children: React.ReactNode;
149	};
150	
151	/**
152	 * Provides the shared cart-drawer state to `children` AND renders `CartDrawerContainer` — the
153	 * component that actually renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` with real basket content — in the same
154	 * place. See this file's own module docblock, constraint 1, for why both happen together here
155	 * rather than leaving `CartDrawerContainer` for some other, easily-forgotten call site to mount.
156	 *
157	 * Written with `React.createElement` rather than JSX so this file can stay `.ts` (as named in
158	 * the SFCC-11 plan's own file manifest) — every other source file under `overrides/app/hooks/`
159	 * is `.ts` with no JSX in it; `useUiCopy.ts`'s own Provider is a separate `.tsx` component under
160	 * `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` rather than living in the hook file itself, which
161	 * is the established split this codebase already uses for exactly this shape. Splitting
162	 * `CartDrawerProvider` out the same way was the more consistent option but would have meant
163	 * creating a file outside this step's own manifest — flagged in the PR report, not decided
164	 * silently. `React.createElement(...)` has one direct precedent already in this codebase for
165	 * the identical reason (a `.ts` file needing to produce a React element without JSX syntax):
166	 * `overrides/app/components/forms/useAddressFields.test.ts:26`.
167	 */
168	export const CartDrawerProvider = ({ value, children }: CartDrawerProviderProps): React.ReactElement =>
169	  React.createElement(
170	    CartDrawerContext.Provider,
171	    { value },
172	    children,
173	    React.createElement(CartDrawerContainer, {
174	      isOpen: value.isOpen,
175	      onClose: value.onClose,
176	      finalFocusRef: value.triggerRef,
177	    }),
178	  );

8	 *     in Storybook; {} signals browser mode, same pattern as header/index.stories.tsx)
9	 *   MultiSiteProvider — StoreLocatorProvider → useMultiSite (reads site.id for localStorage key)
10	 *   CommerceApiProvider + QueryClientProvider — useShopperBasketsV2Mutation, useSFPayments,

12	 *   CurrencyProvider — useCurrency (reads CurrencyContext, separate from CommerceApiProvider)
13	 *   StoreLocatorProvider — useSelectedStore (reads selected store state)

17	 * for the full rationale on this provider pattern.

20	import { expect, fn, userEvent, within } from 'storybook/test';
21	import React from 'react';
22	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
23	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';

38	});

40	// Inert store-locator config — no real BOPIS API calls in Storybook.

51	const CommerceProviders = ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => (
52	  <QueryClientProvider client={storybookQueryClient}>
53	    <CommerceApiProvider
54	      clientId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
55	      organizationId="f_ecom_storybook_001"
56	      shortCode="storybook"
57	      siteId="ZimmermannAU"

65	      {/* useCurrency reads from CurrencyContext; useAddToCartModalContext reads from
66	          AddToCartModalContext; useSelectedStore reads from StoreLocatorContext —
67	          none of these are covered by CommerceApiProvider. */}
68	      <CurrencyProvider currency="AUD">

151	  title: 'Commerce/ProductView',
152	  component: ProductView,
153	  decorators: [WithProviders],
154	  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
155	  args: {
156	    product: MOCK_PRODUCT_WITH_SIZE,

187	export const Default: Story = {

1	import { createContext, useContext } from 'react';
2	
3	export type UiCopyContextValue = {
4	  /**
5	   * Returns the CMS value for `key`, or `fallback` while the fetch is loading, on fetch
6	   * error, or when no `uiCopy` entry with that key exists yet. When `values` is passed,
7	   * every `{token}` in the resolved string (CMS value or fallback) is replaced from it —
8	   * mirrors react-intl's `formatMessage(descriptor, values)` shape closely enough that a
9	   * call site converting away from react-intl only has to change the function, not the
10	   * string template itself.
11	   */
12	  t: (key: string, fallback: string, values?: Record<string, string | number>) => string;
13	  isLoading: boolean;
14	};
15	
16	/**
17	 * Replaces every `{token}` in `template` with `values[token]`, left untouched if `token`
18	 * isn't in `values`. Shared by both the real UiCopyProvider and FALLBACK_ONLY below so a
19	 * key with no matching Contentful entry still interpolates correctly against its fallback.
20	 */
21	export const interpolateUiCopy = (template: string, values?: Record<string, string | number>): string => {
22	  if (!values) return template;
23	  return template.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (match, token: string) => (token in values ? String(values[token]) : match));
24	};
25	
26	/**
27	 * Populated by UiCopyProvider (overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider), mounted once in
28	 * _app-config. Not meant to be consumed directly — call useUiCopy() instead, which supplies
29	 * the no-Provider fallback.
30	 */
31	export const UiCopyContext = createContext<UiCopyContextValue | undefined>(undefined);
32	
33	const FALLBACK_ONLY: UiCopyContextValue = {
34	  t: (_key: string, fallback: string, values?: Record<string, string | number>) => interpolateUiCopy(fallback, values),
35	  isLoading: false,
36	};
37	
38	/**
39	 * App-wide UI-copy lookup, backed by Contentful's uiCopy content type — one entry per string,
40	 * fetched in a single bulk call by UiCopyProvider and shared via context, the same pattern
41	 * this app already uses for translations (`useIntl`) rather than the per-page container-fetch
42	 * pattern commerce-sdk-react hooks use. uiCopy is app-wide static content, not page-specific
43	 * business data, so it's safe to call from any component — including presentational leaves —
44	 * without threading it through as a prop.
45	 *
46	 * Safe to call with no UiCopyProvider mounted above it (Storybook, an isolated unit test):
47	 * degrades to fallback-only text instead of throwing, so every call site stays functional and
48	 * testable with zero setup.
49	 *
50	 * @returns `t` lookup function plus `isLoading`
51	 */
52	export const useUiCopy = (): UiCopyContextValue => useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;

1	import React, { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
2	import type { RefObject } from 'react';
3	import { useDisclosure } from '@chakra-ui/react';
4	import { useLocation } from 'react-router-dom';
5	import logger from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/logger-instance';
6	import { CartDrawerContainer } from 'app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer';
7	
8	/*
9	 * SFCC-11 plan step 9 (final commit) — mirrors the shape of base's own
10	 * `use-add-to-cart-modal.js` (a state-builder hook + a Context Provider + a Context-reading
11	 * hook), but simpler in one real, verified way: unlike base's modal, this drawer takes no
12	 * "item added" payload at all — across all 17 Figma state groups there is no "just added" state,
13	 * the drawer always renders whatever the current basket contains (see `CartDrawerContainer`'s own
14	 * docblock). So the shared state here is just isOpen/onOpen/onClose, and Chakra's own
15	 * `useDisclosure()` — already used for exactly this shape elsewhere in this codebase
16	 * (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:126`) — is the more idiomatic choice than hand-rolling base's raw
17	 * `useState`.
18	 *
19	 * Two real constraints shaped this file, both found by reading the actual current code rather
20	 * than assumed:
21	 *
22	 * 1. **The structural trap base's own code fell into.** `AddToCartModalProvider` is mounted in
23	 *    base `_app` today, but `<AddToCartModal />` itself is never rendered anywhere, base or
24	 *    override (confirmed by grepping the whole `retail-react-app` package) — a component can't
25	 *    easily be both a Context's wrapper and a Context's consumer of its own child in the same
26	 *    render pass, and base's own code never solved that, so add-to-cart has shipped with zero
27	 *    visual feedback. Fixed here by making `CartDrawerProvider` itself render
28	 *    `CartDrawerContainer` (the file that actually renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` with real basket
29	 *    content) — the Provider can never be mounted without the real UI being fed real props,
30	 *    because both happen in the same component body.
31	 *
32	 * 2. **`_app` needs this same live state for its own bag-icon click handler, and `_app` is the
33	 *    component that mounts `CartDrawerProvider`.** A component cannot consume a context it is
34	 *    itself providing within its own subtree — there is no ancestor `CartDrawerProvider` above
35	 *    `_app`'s own top-level code, only a descendant one it's about to render. `useCartDrawerState`
36	 *    is exported separately from `useCartDrawer` so `_app` can call the *raw* state builder
37	 *    directly (the same way it already calls plain `useDisclosure()` directly for its own mobile
38	 *    nav drawer state) and pass the resulting value into `<CartDrawerProvider value={...}>` —
39	 *    so `_app`'s own handler and every nested consumer (`product-view`) always observe the
40	 *    identical live state, never two independent copies. `useCartDrawer()` (the Context reader)
41	 *    is for every other consumer, which — unlike `_app` — genuinely is a descendant of the
42	 *    Provider.
43	 */
44	
45	export type CartDrawerContextValue = {
46	  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
47	  isOpen: boolean;
48	  /**
49	   * Opens the drawer. Pass the element that should receive focus back once the drawer closes
50	   * (AC10) — e.g. the real clicked `<button>`/`<IconButton>` DOM node. Mirrors
51	   * `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `handleTriggerClick` (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:267-276`):
52	   * capture a real element at the moment of the triggering interaction, rather than reading
53	   * `document.activeElement` later — that file's own comment on why
54	   * (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:268-269`) applies identically here: a mouse click does not
55	   * reliably focus the clicked element in every browser. Omit/pass `null`/`undefined` when no
56	   * trigger element is available; the previous trigger (if any) is left untouched rather than
57	   * cleared, so a best-effort focus target is still preferred over none.
58	   */
59	  onOpen: (trigger?: HTMLElement | null) => void;
60	  /** Closes the drawer. Does not clear `triggerRef` — see `handleCloseComplete` in
61	   *  `zimmDrawer/index.tsx`, which reads `finalFocusRef` only after the close animation
62	   *  finishes, i.e. strictly after `onClose` has already run. Clearing the ref here would
63	   *  make AC10 focus-return silently fail on every close. */
64	  onClose: () => void;
65	  /** AC10 focus-return target — whichever element was last passed to `onOpen`. Forward to
66	   *  `ZimmDrawer`/`CartDrawerContainer`'s `finalFocusRef` prop. Typed as `RefObject<HTMLElement>`
67	   *  (not `| null`) to satisfy that prop's own type — same typing precedent as
68	   *  `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `triggerRef` (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:88,140`). */
69	  triggerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement>;
70	};
71	
72	// Exported (not just used internally) for the same reason base exports `AddToCartModalContext`
73	// directly (`use-add-to-cart-modal.js:59`) — lets a test wrap a subtree with a controlled value
74	// via `CartDrawerContext.Provider` directly, without going through the real state builder.
75	export const CartDrawerContext = createContext<CartDrawerContextValue | undefined>(undefined);
76	
77	/**
78	 * Builds the cart drawer's shared isOpen/onOpen/onClose state plus its AC10 focus-return
79	 * trigger ref — the raw equivalent of base's own `useAddToCartModal()`. Called exactly once, by
80	 * `_app`, which passes the result into `CartDrawerProvider`'s `value` prop — see this file's own
81	 * module docblock (constraint 2) for why `_app` needs the raw builder rather than
82	 * `useCartDrawer()`'s Context read.
83	 *
84	 * @returns The shared cart-drawer state — see `CartDrawerContextValue`.
85	 */
86	export const useCartDrawerState = (): CartDrawerContextValue => {
87	  const { isOpen, onOpen: onDisclosureOpen, onClose } = useDisclosure();
88	  // Typed as HTMLElement (not HTMLElement | null) so `.current` is writable below — same cast
89	  // and reasoning as useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:140 (a plain `useRef<HTMLElement>(null)` would
90	  // infer the read-only `RefObject<HTMLElement>` overload instead of `MutableRefObject`).
91	  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null as unknown as HTMLElement);
92	
93	  const onOpen = (trigger?: HTMLElement | null): void => {
94	    if (trigger) triggerRef.current = trigger;
95	    onDisclosureOpen();
96	  };
97	
98	  // Judgement call (no AC or Figma state describes this either way — see this hook's own
99	  // module docblock and the PR report for the fuller reasoning): close the drawer whenever the
100	  // route changes, mirroring base `use-add-to-cart-modal.js`'s own `[pathname]`-keyed effect
101	  // (`use-add-to-cart-modal.js:603-611`) and this exact file's sibling precedent —
102	  // `_app/index.tsx`'s own mobile-nav drawer already closes itself the same way
103	  // (`_app/index.tsx`'s own `useEffect(() => { onClose(); }, [location])`, "Lets automatically
104	  // close the mobile navigation when the location path is changed."). Concretely load-bearing,
105	  // not just consistency: `ZimmCartButtonGroup`'s Checkout button (already built, SFCC-275)
106	  // navigates via a plain `history.push('/checkout')` with no `onClose` call of its own
107	  // (verified directly against `zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx`'s `handleCheckoutClick`), and
108	  // `ZimmDrawer`'s overlay is not click-through — without this effect, clicking Checkout from
109	  // inside the cart drawer would navigate to `/checkout` while the drawer stayed open on top of
110	  // it, leaving the shopper unable to see or reach the page they just navigated to.
111	  const { pathname } = useLocation();
112	  useEffect(() => {
113	    if (isOpen) {
114	      onClose();
115	    }
116	    // Deliberately keyed on pathname alone, matching use-add-to-cart-modal.js's own shape —
117	    // isOpen/onClose are read for their current value, not to decide when the effect re-runs.
118	  }, [pathname]);
119	
120	  return { isOpen, onOpen, onClose, triggerRef };
121	};
122	
123	// Stable (module-level, not per-render) no-op fallback for when no CartDrawerProvider is
124	// mounted above the caller — see useCartDrawer's own doc for why this degrades instead of
125	// throwing. `triggerRef` is a plain inert object, not a real useRef() result: nothing outside a
126	// real CartDrawerProvider subtree ever reads it back for a real focus call.
127	const FALLBACK_ONLY: CartDrawerContextValue = {
128	  isOpen: false,
129	  onOpen: () => {
130	    // A real shopper's page always has a CartDrawerProvider ancestor (mounted once in `_app`),
131	    // so reaching this in a real request is a genuine bug, not an expected path — logged so a
132	    // silently-broken Add to Bag button is at least observable, rather than a shopper clicking
133	    // it and nothing happening with no trace anywhere.
134	    logger.warn('useCartDrawer called with no CartDrawerProvider mounted — Add to Bag will not open the cart drawer.', {
135	      namespace: 'useCartDrawer',
136	    });
137	  },
138	  onClose: () => undefined,
139	  triggerRef: { current: null },
140	};
141	
142	/**
143	 * Reads the shared cart-drawer state from Context. For any consumer that is a genuine descendant
144	 * of `CartDrawerProvider` (e.g. `product-view`) — see this file's own module docblock for why
145	 * `_app` itself must use `useCartDrawerState()` directly instead.
146	 *
147	 * Degrades to a stable, harmless no-op outside a Provider — the same shape `useUiCopy.ts` already
148	 * uses (`useContext(...) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`) — rather than throwing. Confirmed necessary, not
149	 * merely convenient: `product-view/index.stories.tsx` (unmodified by this change — not in this
150	 * step's own manifest) wraps `ProductView`'s stories in the now-removed `AddToCartModalProvider`,
151	 * with no `CartDrawerProvider` in its own decorator stack, and every one of its stories renders
152	 * the real default `ProductView` export, which calls this hook unconditionally near its own top
153	 * level. A throwing `useCartDrawer` (this file's own first draft, matching `useIntl`'s
154	 * load-bearing/non-degrading precedent) crashes all four of that file's stories on mount, before
155	 * any interaction — verified live against a real running Storybook instance, not assumed (see
156	 * this step's own PR report). `onOpen`'s own no-op additionally logs a warning (see
157	 * `FALLBACK_ONLY` above) so a genuine missing-Provider bug in the real app — which should never
158	 * happen, since `_app` always mounts one — is still observable rather than a silent dead button.
159	 *
160	 * @returns The shared cart-drawer state — see `CartDrawerContextValue`.
161	 */
162	export const useCartDrawer = (): CartDrawerContextValue => useContext(CartDrawerContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;
163	
164	export type CartDrawerProviderProps = {
165	  /** The live state to provide — built via `useCartDrawerState()` by the one caller (`_app`)
166	   *  that also needs it directly for its own bag-icon click handler. Accepting it as a prop
167	   *  (rather than calling `useCartDrawerState()` internally) is what lets `_app` and every
168	   *  nested consumer share the exact same instance — see this file's own module docblock,
169	   *  constraint 2. */
170	  value: CartDrawerContextValue;
171	  children: React.ReactNode;
172	};
173	
174	/**
175	 * Provides the shared cart-drawer state to `children` AND renders `CartDrawerContainer` — the
176	 * component that actually renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` with real basket content — in the same
177	 * place. See this file's own module docblock, constraint 1, for why both happen together here
178	 * rather than leaving `CartDrawerContainer` for some other, easily-forgotten call site to mount.
179	 *
180	 * Written with `React.createElement` rather than JSX so this file can stay `.ts` (as named in
181	 * the SFCC-11 plan's own file manifest) — every other source file under `overrides/app/hooks/`
182	 * is `.ts` with no JSX in it; `useUiCopy.ts`'s own Provider is a separate `.tsx` component under
183	 * `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` rather than living in the hook file itself, which
184	 * is the established split this codebase already uses for exactly this shape. Splitting
185	 * `CartDrawerProvider` out the same way was the more consistent option but would have meant
186	 * creating a file outside this step's own manifest — flagged in the PR report, not decided
187	 * silently. `React.createElement(...)` has one direct precedent already in this codebase for
188	 * the identical reason (a `.ts` file needing to produce a React element without JSX syntax):
189	 * `overrides/app/components/forms/useAddressFields.test.ts:26`.
190	 */
191	export const CartDrawerProvider = ({ value, children }: CartDrawerProviderProps): React.ReactElement =>
192	  React.createElement(
193	    CartDrawerContext.Provider,
194	    { value },
195	    children,
196	    React.createElement(CartDrawerContainer, {
197	      isOpen: value.isOpen,
198	      onClose: value.onClose,
199	      finalFocusRef: value.triggerRef,
200	    }),
201	  );
